title: Darjeeling vs Gangtok: which to pick for a first trip
meta_description: Darjeeling or Gangtok for a first hill trip? We compare views, permits, cost, food, day trips and seasons, and say when to do both in 5 or 6 nights.
summary: For a first trip with only 3 nights, pick Darjeeling if you want tea gardens, the toy train and a Kangchenjunga sunrise; pick Gangtok if you want a cleaner, calmer town and a day at a high lake. With 5 or 6 nights, do both: 2–3 nights each, linked by a 4–5 hour road.
key_takeaways: Darjeeling is the better pick for views, history, tea and the toy train; Gangtok wins on tidy streets, food and high-altitude day trips.
Both are about 3–5 hours by road from Siliguri, and the drive between them takes 4–5 hours, so a 5-night combined trip works well.
Indian citizens need no permit for either town; Tsomgo and Nathu La from Gangtok need a protected area permit, arranged through a registered agent.
Costs are close: a budget couple spends roughly ₹2,000–3,000 a person a day in either town, indicative 2026.

sections.heading: The short answer
paras: We get this question more than any other, usually from a family in Kolkata or Bengaluru with one week of leave and a first hill trip in mind. Our honest answer is that the two towns are less alike than they look on a map. Darjeeling is an old Bengal hill station on a narrow ridge, built around tea, schools and a railway. Gangtok is the capital of a state that was a separate kingdom until 1975, and it runs like one: wide promenades, rules about litter and smoking, and a busy permit office for the high passes.

If you only have 3 nights, pick one town and do it properly. If you have 5 or 6 nights, do both. The road between them is about 95–100 km and takes 4–5 hours by car, through Teesta Bazaar or via Kalimpong, so it eats one morning but not a whole day.

paras: Here is how the two compare on the things first-timers ask us about. Prices are indicative for 2026 and rise in May, June and the October holidays.

sections.heading: Pick Darjeeling if you want this
paras: Darjeeling gives you more to do on foot, and more history per square kilometre, than any other town in these hills. The Chowrasta and the Mall are a short walk from most hotels. Within a few hours you can stand at the Batasia Loop, visit the Yiga Choeling monastery at Ghum, watch a steam engine take water, and drink a first-flush tea in the town where it is grown. The Himalayan Mountaineering Institute and the zoo next door are a morning in themselves.

The big draw is Kangchenjunga at 8,586 m. From October to December the mountain fills the northern sky on most mornings, and the sunrise from Tiger Hill, 11 km out of town, is the classic first-trip memory. You also get tea: half a day at an estate near Kurseong or at Happy Valley costs little and explains more about the region than any museum.

The catch is that Darjeeling is crowded and steep. Traffic on Hill Cart Road crawls in peak weeks, the old town has many stairs, and cheaper hotels below the Mall can mean a steep walk back after dinner. Seniors should book close to Chowrasta even if it costs ₹500–1,000 more a night.
list: Best for: tea lovers, railway fans, photographers, families with school-age children
Do not miss: Tiger Hill on a clear morning, the joy ride to Ghum, a tea estate walk
Skip if: you dislike crowds or have knee trouble and cannot stay near the Mall

sections.heading: Pick Gangtok if you want this
paras: Gangtok suits people who want a town that works. MG Marg, the main promenade, is closed to vehicles, has no spitting or smoking allowed, and fills with families after dark. Food is better and wider than in Darjeeling: momos, thukpa, Sikkimese thali, Tibetan bakeries and good Bengali and North Indian kitchens for the less adventurous.

The signature day out is the drive to Tsomgo Lake at about 3,750 m and the Baba Harbhajan Singh Mandir, with Nathu La on the Indo-China border on the days it is open to visitors. These need a protected area permit, which a registered Gangtok travel agent arranges for you a day ahead with photo ID and photos. Check current status before you travel, because the road closes after heavy snow or landslides.
Gangtok is also the base for North Sikkim: Lachung, Yumthang and Lachen. Many first-timers who choose Gangtok end up adding two nights up north, which needs another permit and a package vehicle.
list: Best for: couples, food lovers, travellers who want snow and high lakes
Do not miss: an evening on MG Marg, Rumtek monastery, Tsomgo Lake
Skip if: you will not go beyond the town, since the high-altitude trips are the main reason to come

sections.heading: When to do both, and how
paras: Five nights is the sweet spot for a first trip that covers both towns. We usually suggest 2 nights in Darjeeling and 3 in Gangtok, because the Tsomgo day needs a permit and a spare day in case the road shuts. Start in Darjeeling if you are arriving at NJP by train, since it is the closer town; start in Gangtok if you fly into Bagdogra in the morning and want to end with the toy train.

On a budget, the transfer between the towns costs ₹400–600 a seat in a shared jeep or ₹4,000–5,500 for a small reserved car, indicative 2026. With four people the reserved car is better value, and you can stop at the Teesta river viewpoint where the Teesta and Rangeet meet, on the Peshok road.

Our 5-night honeymoon and 6-night family packages follow exactly this plan. A budget version of 5 nights covering both towns starts around ₹16,000 per person on twin sharing, comfort around ₹27,000, indicative 2026.

sections.heading: Seasons change the answer
paras: In October and November both towns are at their best, and both are at their busiest. If you can travel only in Durga Puja week, book early and think about Gangtok, which handles crowds better on its pedestrian streets.

In winter, from December to February, Darjeeling has the clearest views but is cold, around 2–9 °C, and many small hotels cut back on hot water. Gangtok is a few degrees warmer, and the drive to Tsomgo can bring snow, which is the main reason many families pick Sikkim in January.

In the monsoon, from mid-June to mid-September, Darjeeling is often lost in cloud and the toy train can be suspended after landslides. Gangtok is a little better placed, with more indoor sights and good food, but the Tsomgo road and the North Sikkim routes can close for days. Monsoon is the cheapest time in both towns, with hotel discounts of 30–50 percent.

sections.heading: What first-timers get wrong
paras: The most common mistake is trying to squeeze both towns into 3 nights. You spend two of your days in a car, see Kangchenjunga through a windscreen, and go home tired. The second is treating Tiger Hill as a must on the first morning, when you have just arrived from the plains. Leave it for your second or third morning and check the sky the night before; if the forecast is cloudy, sleep in and go to Ghum later.

The third mistake is booking a reserved car for every leg. In both towns, local shared taxis and jeeps cover short hops for ₹20–150 a seat. Use a reserved car for Tiger Hill and Tsomgo, where you need one, and ride with the locals the rest of the time. That alone can save a couple ₹4,000–6,000 over five nights.

faqs.q: Is Darjeeling or Gangtok better for a first trip
faqs.a: With 3 nights, pick Darjeeling for tea, the toy train and the Kangchenjunga sunrise, or Gangtok for a cleaner town, better food and a day at Tsomgo Lake. With 5 or 6 nights, do both: the drive between them is 4–5 hours and costs ₹400–600 a seat in a shared jeep, indicative 2026.

faqs.q: How many days are enough for Darjeeling and Gangtok together
faqs.a: Five nights is the minimum we suggest: 2 in Darjeeling and 3 in Gangtok, so you have a spare day if the Tsomgo road closes. Six nights is more relaxed for families and seniors. Trying to fit both towns into 3 nights means most of your time is spent in a car on hill roads.

faqs.q: Do Indians need a permit for Gangtok
faqs.a: No permit is needed for Indian citizens to visit Gangtok town or Darjeeling. You do need a protected area permit for Tsomgo Lake, Baba Mandir and Nathu La, arranged by a registered travel agent with photo ID and passport photos, usually a day ahead. Rules change, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Which is colder, Darjeeling or Gangtok
faqs.a: Darjeeling is colder because it sits higher, at about 2,040 m against Gangtok's 1,650 m. In January, Darjeeling is roughly 2–9 °C and Gangtok a few degrees warmer. Snow is rare in both towns, but the drive to Tsomgo Lake from Gangtok often reaches snow between December and March.

faqs.q: Which town is cheaper, Darjeeling or Gangtok
faqs.a: They cost about the same. A budget traveller sharing a room spends roughly ₹2,000–3,000 a day in either town, indicative 2026. Gangtok's extra costs are the Tsomgo or North Sikkim vehicle and permit; Darjeeling's are the Tiger Hill car and the toy train joy ride. Monsoon brings the deepest hotel discounts in both.
